Description:
Defines weather data tailored to the decisions made by Libertas applications.
The sprinkler schema persists its Hub-provided site location separately from recent history, current conditions, and forecast data. Each weather section has a different refresh interval and may succeed or fail independently. Runtime snapshots may contain any combination of sections. Applications persist each successful section separately and retain older sections when a weather-data refresh fails. Incremental subscriptions use epoch-timestamp-and-sequence cursors so clients can distinguish a server cursor reset from stale or out-of-order data, replay retained changes, or recover selected time ranges from cached data.
The building-HVAC schema supplies only the outdoor inputs needed for thermal load prediction, heat-pump operation, economizer decisions, and controlled outdoor-air ventilation. It keeps weather and outdoor-air-quality sections independent because they have different providers and freshness behavior. Local equipment and life-safety controls must continue to use their own sensors; cached internet weather is supervisory input, not a safety signal.

When the server loses its transient cursor or replay journal, it assigns an epoch timestamp strictly newer than the previous one and starts `sequence` again at zero. A client can first observe a later post-reset sequence rather than zero. This timestamp describes cursor state, not the observation time of weather values.

List.Name: Sequence
List.Description: Identifies the latest applied state change. The server increments this value once for every accepted weather change. It resets this value to zero when the transient server cursor is reset, then increments it for later changes; a reset does not clear historical, current, or forecast weather data.

Types.Name: SprinklerWeatherForecastPeriodV1

List.Description: Contains predicted water input, water loss, temperature, humidity, and wind hazards used to decide when and how much to water during one planning period.

List.Name: Temperature

List.Name: Relative humidity
List.Description: Predicted relative humidity at two meters above ground, expressed as an integer percentage from 0 through 100. Together with solar position and sprinkler-head type, this helps avoid prolonged foliage wetness.

List.Name: Precipitation probability
List.Description: Probability of measurable precipitation during this period, expressed as an integer percentage from 0 through 100. This expresses forecast uncertainty separately from expected precipitation amount.

List.Name: Expected precipitation
List.Description: Predicted total rain, showers, and water-equivalent frozen precipitation accumulated during this period in millimeters.

List.Name: Reference evapotranspiration
List.Description: Predicted FAO-56 reference evapotranspiration accumulated during this period in millimeters.

List.Name: Wind speed
List.Description: Predicted sustained wind speed at 10 meters above ground in meters per second.

List.Name: Wind gust
List.Description: Predicted peak wind gust speed at 10 meters above ground in meters per second. The sprinkler uses this with sustained wind to avoid scheduling watering during likely spray drift.

Types.Name: SprinklerWeatherIncrementalReportV1
Types.Description: Carries an ordered, atomic range of weather changes. A client applies the report only when its stored cursor equals `from_cursor`, then stores `through_cursor`. An empty report is a caught-up recovery result; periodic no-change liveness uses PeerAlive.

List.Name: Sprinkler weather incremental report
List.Description: Carries an ordered, atomic range of weather changes. A client applies the report only when its stored cursor equals `from_cursor`, then stores `through_cursor`. An empty report is a caught-up recovery result; periodic no-change liveness uses PeerAlive.

List.Name: From cursor
List.Description: The exclusive lower cursor for this report and the exact cursor a client must already hold before applying it.

List.Name: Through cursor
List.Description: The inclusive upper cursor reached after applying every change in this report. It must retain the same epoch timestamp as `from_cursor`. A server cursor reset is never carried as an incremental report; it requires a full reset.

List.Name: Weather changes
List.Description: Ordered changes to apply atomically. Each item advances the sequence by exactly one; an empty list is caught-up recovery and does not advance the cursor or serve as periodic liveness.

List.Name: Weather change
List.Description: One atomic state mutation in cursor order.

Types.Name: SprinklerWeatherProtocol
Types.Description: Defines the typed Libertas endpoint transaction for requesting or subscribing to sprinkler weather. Responses expose independently available history, current, and forecast sections so an outage does not hide usable cached data. The Libertas endpoint status contract rejects malformed Avro and values used in the wrong message role; those transport errors are not recovery variants.

List.Name: Sprinkler weather protocol
List.Description: Defines the typed Libertas endpoint transaction for requesting or subscribing to sprinkler weather. Responses expose independently available history, current, and forecast sections so an outage does not hide usable cached data. The Libertas endpoint status contract rejects malformed Avro and values used in the wrong message role; those transport errors are not recovery variants.

List.Name: Get sprinkler weather
List.Description: Performs a one-shot incremental read or starts or resumes an incremental subscription. The Libertas endpoint operation selects the behavior; it is not encoded in this message. The server replays retained changes after `after_cursor` when possible, or returns a range-limited cached snapshot.

List.Name: Resume cursor
List.Description: The last cursor fully and atomically applied by the client. `None` requests an initial range-limited snapshot. The server compares both fields; a lower sequence indicates a reset only when the response cursor also has a newer epoch timestamp.

List.Name: Historical recovery range
List.Description: The half-open range of historical period start times to include when replay is impossible. `None` excludes history from the reset snapshot.

List.Name: Include current conditions
List.Description: Whether a reset snapshot should include cached current conditions.

List.Name: Forecast recovery range
List.Description: The half-open range of forecast period start times to include when replay is impossible. `None` excludes forecast data from the reset snapshot.

List.Name: Sprinkler weather recovery
List.Description: Responds to a weather request with replayed changes, a reset snapshot, or a recoverable error. Every response supplies a maximum wait interval. A subscription client uses it after a successful replay or reset; a one-shot client ignores it. After an error, the recovery error and retry delay take precedence.

List.Name: Maximum wait interval
List.Description: The maximum number of seconds a subscription client waits after a successful recovery, incremental report, or PeerAlive. The server sends changed data or PeerAlive first. One-shot clients ignore this required, nonzero value.

List.Name: Recovery
List.Description: The replay, reset, or error result for the resume request.

List.Name: Sprinkler weather increment
List.Description: Reports only state changes after a successful weather request. A cursor mismatch or non-contiguous range requires another subscription request; the client must not apply the report partially. A valid report or PeerAlive restarts the recovery response's wait timer; PeerAlive never enters this data schema or changes the cursor.

List.Name: Incremental report
List.Description: The ordered atomic cursor range and its weather changes.

Types.Name: SprinklerWeatherRecoveryErrorV1
Types.Description: Identifies a recovery request that cannot be satisfied with either replayed changes or a range-limited cached snapshot.

List.Name: Sprinkler weather recovery error
List.Description: Identifies a recovery request that cannot be satisfied with either replayed changes or a range-limited cached snapshot.

Enum.Name: Invalid time range
Enum.Description: At least one requested half-open time range is empty or reversed.

Enum.Name: Cursor ahead
Enum.Description: The supplied epoch-timestamp-and-sequence cursor cannot be reconciled with the server's current cursor or retained replay journal.

Enum.Name: Request too large
Enum.Description: The requested recovery ranges exceed the server's bounded response capacity.

Enum.Name: Temporarily unavailable
Enum.Description: Cached data or another required recovery resource is temporarily unavailable; the client may retry after the supplied delay.

Types.Name: SprinklerWeatherRecoveryV1
Types.Description: Returns replayed changes, establishes a new cursor with a range-limited snapshot, or reports a recoverable request error.

List.Name: Sprinkler weather recovery
List.Description: Returns replayed changes, establishes a new cursor with a range-limited snapshot, or reports a recoverable request error.

List.Name: Replayed changes
List.Description: Continues the requested stream by replaying every retained change after the supplied cursor. An empty report means the client is already caught up.

List.Name: Incremental report
List.Description: The contiguous change range beginning at the requested cursor.

List.Name: Recovery error
List.Description: Rejects the request without changing the client's cursor or local weather state.

List.Name: Error
List.Description: The reason recovery could not be completed.

List.Name: Retry delay
List.Description: The suggested delay in seconds before retrying. `None` means the request parameters must change before a retry can succeed.

List.Name: Reset with site snapshot V2
List.Description: Establishes a new cursor and binds a full-observation history snapshot to its provider site.

List.Name: Reset reason
List.Description: The reason a snapshot replaced incremental replay.

List.Name: Current cursor
List.Description: The cursor representing the returned snapshot.

List.Name: Site location
List.Description: WGS84 location used to obtain the returned weather sections.

List.Name: Weather snapshot
List.Description: Available V2 cached sections constrained by requested ranges.

Types.Name: SprinklerWeatherResetReasonV1
Types.Description: Explains why recovery returned a range-limited snapshot instead of replaying incremental changes after the requested cursor.

List.Name: Sprinkler weather reset reason
List.Description: Explains why recovery returned a range-limited snapshot instead of replaying incremental changes after the requested cursor.

Enum.Name: Initial subscription
Enum.Description: No prior cursor was supplied, so the snapshot establishes initial state.

Enum.Name: Cursor expired
Enum.Description: The requested sequence is older than the retained replay journal.

Enum.Name: Server cursor reset
Enum.Description: The server lost or deliberately discarded only its transient cursor and replay journal. Persisted weather sections remain usable, and missing historical data can be retrieved again from Open-Meteo.
